summary: The requested marker content and its test are present and the supplied deterministic validation passed, but compatibility across the project’s supported Node versions is not established.

checks.name: Correctness
checks.evidence: MARKER.md changes from the required start line to exactly two ordered, newline-terminated lines. tests/marker.test.mjs asserts the full line array equals those two values, and the supplied validation output reports that subtest passing.

checks.name: Failure handling
checks.evidence: The executable addition only synchronously reads MARKER.md and performs assertions; it creates no persistent state or external side effects. A read or assertion failure terminates the test without partially modifying repository state.

checks.name: State and concurrency
checks.evidence: The changed runtime test, tests/marker.test.mjs, only reads MARKER.md and uses no shared mutable state, asynchronous work, persistence, or concurrency.

checks.name: Security and authority
checks.evidence: tests/marker.test.mjs uses fixed repository-relative path MARKER.md and Node built-ins only; the patch adds no credentials, command execution, user-controlled input, permissions, or authority boundary.

checks.name: Compatibility
checks.evidence: tests/marker.test.mjs uses Array.prototype.at(-1), which requires a sufficiently recent Node.js runtime. The supplied successful validation proves one unspecified Node environment worked, but supplies no supported-Node-version policy or Linux CI runtime evidence.

checks.name: Tests
checks.evidence: The patch adds tests/marker.test.mjs, which reads MARKER.md and asserts both exact lines in order and the trailing newline. The deterministic validation for node scripts/check-rehearsal.mjs exited 0 and recorded the matching TAP subtest as passing.

residualRisks: Confirm the project’s supported Node.js versions include Array.prototype.at, or replace it with a compatibility-safe equivalent.
